_note: Retain / release calls for the IPL 2027 retention window. Numbers come from the supplied ball-by-ball data (2022-26) and scripts/06_rr_squad.py; 'pct' = percentile among ranked specialists. Written 16 Nov 2026, before the official lists.

needs.need: A second strike bowler, ideally one who holds up at the death
needs.evidence: Archer took 25 wickets but concedes 9.6 an over on pressure balls against 8.9 otherwise (lift 2nd percentile). Deshpande, Sandeep Sharma, Burger and Milne all went at 10+ in 2026.

needs.need: A middle-order batter who scores against spin under pressure
needs.evidence: Parag (135 strike rate under pressure v 156 otherwise), Jurel (132 v 157) and Hetmyer (average 17 under pressure) all dip; Jurel and Hetmyer strike at about 130 against spin.

needs.need: A frontline spinner to replace or share with Jadeja
needs.evidence: Jadeja is 38 in December and missed games injured; Bishnoi has gone at 10.8 and 9.9 in the last two IPL seasons.

50284.headline: The best pressure batter in the entire dataset, at Rs 1.1 crore.
reasons: Ranked No. 1 of 111 batters under pressure; he tops the list in essentially every resample of his matches.
IPL 2026: 776 runs at a strike rate of 238 (Orange Cap). On pressure balls he averages 79 at a strike rate of 240.
Model value about Rs 31 crore a season against a Rs 1.1 crore salary: the largest surplus on any contract we can see.
50284.watch: Only 673 balls of evidence and he is 15: manage workload and expect bowlers to adjust.

6819.headline: Five straight productive seasons and no pressure dip; expensive but not replaceable.
reasons: 73rd percentile under pressure (28th of 111), strike rate 160 under pressure v 156 otherwise, and a lift in the 92nd percentile: he is one of the few RR batters who does not dip.
400+ runs in each of the last four IPL seasons at 152-164.
At Rs 18 crore the model values his output nearer Rs 10 crore, but an Indian opener of this quality does not reach a mini-auction.
6819.watch: Trade speculation exists; franchise sources say he stays. Average drops from 37 to 32 under pressure even as the strike rate holds.

7260.headline: Keeper and 515 runs in 2026, but the squad's clearest pressure dip.
reasons: IPL 2026: 515 runs, strike rate 155, six fifties; keeps wicket, which the model does not value.
Under pressure his strike rate falls from 159 to 129 and his average from 34 to 23: lift in the 5th percentile, the worst in the squad.
14th percentile overall under pressure, 101st of 111. Output is worth about Rs 6 crore on our scale against a Rs 14 crore salary.
7260.watch: Keep, but do not build the chase around him: pair with a spin-hitter at 4 or 5.

6423.headline: Captain and Indian middle-order core; average under pressure, paid as a star.
reasons: Under pressure: strike rate 148 v 153 otherwise, average 28. Lift in the 18th percentile, 58th percentile overall.
Worth about Rs 6 crore on our scale against Rs 14 crore. Continuity as captain and the lack of a like-for-like Indian replacement at a mini-auction carry the decision.
6423.watch: If results stall, this is the contract to revisit before the 2028 mega auction.

152.headline: Still RR's best bowler when it matters, but Rs 14 crore buys far more at auction.
reasons: Bowling under pressure: economy 7.69 v 7.94 otherwise; 59th percentile with the ball, 43rd of 115.
Batting: 4th percentile of ranked batters under pressure, 102nd of 111, and 128 strike rate when it tightens.
Turns 38 in December and missed games injured in 2026. Output worth about Rs 7 crore against Rs 14 crore.
152.watch: Bold call: only release if the plan is to bid back up to about Rs 7 crore. The safe scenario keeps him.

3298.headline: The only strike bowler: 25 wickets in 2026. Needs a partner for the pressure overs.
reasons: IPL 2026: 25 wickets in 16 matches, 44% dot balls.
67th percentile with the ball, but his lift sits in the 17th: economy 8.82 under pressure against 9.14 otherwise is barely a gain on an already expensive baseline.
Model value (Rs 12.9 crore) matches his Rs 12.5 crore salary.
3298.watch: Do not use him as the sole death option; workload across formats.

8182.headline: The finisher RR already own: strike rate 179 in 2026 for Rs 1 crore.
reasons: IPL 2026: 317 runs at 179, average 35; 206 at the death.
Equally quick against pace (162) and spin (168): the profile the middle order lacks.
88th percentile batting estimate; surplus about Rs 6.7 crore.
8182.watch: Only 34 pressure balls so far: the estimate leans on his overall record.

67036.headline: Uncapped find: 14 wickets in 13 matches at base price.
reasons: IPL 2026: 14 wickets, bowled 297 balls: RR's second-most-used seamer.
Early estimate 82nd percentile, though only 87 pressure balls, so it is heavily shrunk toward average.
Surplus about Rs 10 crore at a Rs 0.3 crore salary.
67036.watch: One season of evidence; economy 10.6 at the death.

7312.headline: Useful left-arm depth at a fair price, not the answer for the second strike bowler.
reasons: IPL 2026: 14 wickets in 13 matches but economy 10.1.
31st percentile under pressure, 76th of 115.
Value (Rs 4.4 crore) roughly matches salary (Rs 3.5 crore); a like-for-like overseas seamer would cost more at auction.
7312.watch: Release becomes right if an overseas slot is needed for a better quick.

41503.headline: 20-year-old leg-spinner who took Bishnoi's place late in the season.
reasons: IPL 2026: 9 wickets in 8 matches, economy 9.3.
Preferred to Bishnoi for the final league game.
Low cost (Rs 0.9 crore), positive surplus.

25139.headline: Cheap Indian middle-order cover.
reasons: 220 IPL runs at 155 across three seasons; 174 at the death.
Strike rate 109 against spin limits the role.
Rs 0.8 crore: replacing him costs about the same.
25139.watch: Is 32; a younger uncapped batter could take the slot.

43798.headline: 20-year-old overseas top-order prospect at base price.
reasons: Since 2025: 1,630 T20 runs at 154 across SA20, internationals and leagues.
Only two IPL games so far.
Rs 0.3 crore; costs an overseas squad slot, not purse.
43798.watch: Predicted as a release by one outlet. Keep only while overseas slots allow (we use 5 of 8).

7269.headline: Left-arm Indian seamer, two games, base price.
reasons: Fewer than 50 IPL balls: too little to judge.
Left-arm angle is scarce among Indian seamers.
Rs 0.3 crore.

48557.headline: Left-arm wrist-spin is rare; costs almost nothing to keep.
reasons: Did not play in 2026; 6 wickets in 72 balls in 2025.
Spin depth matters if Bishnoi is released.
Rs 0.3 crore.

47523.headline: No balls in the data: kept on cost and age alone.
reasons: 22-year-old uncapped batter, did not play in 2026.
No IPL or international deliveries to analyse.
Rs 0.3 crore.
47523.watch: Insufficient data: scouting reports, not this model, should decide.

3297.headline: Rs 11 crore for 78 runs in 2026: the clearest release on the list.
reasons: IPL 2026: 78 runs at a strike rate of 113, average 13; dropped by the last league game.
IPL output has fallen 314 -> 299 -> 113 -> 239 -> 78 runs.
Under pressure he averages 21 against 29 otherwise. Deficit about Rs 9 crore, the largest in the squad.
3297.watch: Still strong in internationals (strike rate 186 since 2025): worth a bid below Rs 4 crore, not a retention.

6806.headline: Economy of 12 in 2026 on a Rs 6.5 crore contract.
reasons: IPL 2026: 4 wickets in 7 matches, economy 12.0.
Economy by season: 9.9, 8.8, 10.6, 12.0.
33rd percentile under pressure, 80th of 115; deficit about Rs 3 crore.

7503.headline: Two poor IPL seasons in a row at Rs 7.2 crore; still a good international bowler.
reasons: IPL economy 10.8 (2025) and 9.9 (2026); dropped after 1 May 2026.
Five-season record is middling (52nd percentile, 63rd of 115), though he has 11 international wickets at an economy of 8.4 since 2025.
Output worth about Rs 4 crore against Rs 7.2 crore.
7503.watch: Rebuy up to about Rs 4 crore; otherwise the money goes to a spinner who bowls the pressure overs.

2411.headline: A fine record that has faded: economy 8.2 -> 9.9 -> 11.4.
reasons: IPL 2026: 5 wickets in 6 matches, economy 11.4.
Five-season quality is good (70th percentile, 39th of 115) but his pressure economy is 9.89 against 8.81 otherwise: lift in the 8th percentile.
Turns 34 in May.
2411.watch: A base-price rebuy as new-ball cover would be reasonable (powerplay economy 7.5).

4409.headline: Missed 2026; below average in both skills in the IPL. Best used in the reported LSG deal.
reasons: Ruled out of IPL 2026 with a groin injury.
IPL bowling economy 10.2, 10.2, 11.1 in his last three seasons; batting strike rate 124-139.
Bowling 25th percentile (84th of 115), batting 21st (70th of 111) under pressure. Uses an overseas slot.
4409.watch: Reported swap for Mohammed Shami is unconfirmed. Shami rates around the middle of the pool under pressure and is 36: useful, not a fix.

2436.headline: Injury replacement who made little impact; 35 years old.
reasons: IPL 2026: 63 runs and 1 wicket in 7 matches.
Mid-table estimates in both skills (64th percentile batting, 47th bowling).
Frees an overseas slot.

1487.headline: One game in 2026 for Rs 2.4 crore.
reasons: IPL 2026: 20 balls, economy 12.3.
27th percentile under pressure, 92nd of 115; 34 years old.
Frees an overseas slot and Rs 2.4 crore.

26663.headline: Talented 20-year-old, but zero games in 2026 and a second left-arm overseas quick.
reasons: Did not play in 2026; 2 wickets in two previous IPL seasons.
Pressure economy 13.3 from 57 balls (small sample).
17 international wickets at an economy of 8.6 since 2025 show the upside.
26663.watch: Could equally be kept as a development player: this one is close.

7545.headline: Did not play in 2026.
reasons: No IPL appearance since 2024 (economy 10.2 that year).
24th percentile estimate, on only 80 pressure balls.
Squad slot is worth more than the Rs 0.75 crore.

8580.headline: No games in 2026; economy 12 in 2025.
reasons: 138 IPL balls at an economy of 11.0.
Bottom-decile estimate (13th percentile).
Rs 0.35 crore: the squad slot matters more than the money.
8580.watch: One report says RR intend to retain him; our numbers do not support it, but the stakes are small.

60700.headline: Withdrew injured after one game; no evidence to justify Rs 0.95 crore.
reasons: Two balls faced in IPL 2026.
No other deliveries in the data.
Rs 0.95 crore is high for an untested uncapped player.

43965.headline: Replacement signing who did not play; nothing to analyse.
reasons: No deliveries in the supplied data or Cricsheet.
Replacement contract for 2026.
Squad slot.

recommended.label: Recommended
recommended.note: Release the declining contracts, rebuy Jadeja and Bishnoi only at lower prices.

safe.label: Safe
safe.note: As recommended, but keep Jadeja and Bishnoi on current contracts.

lessons.title: RR 2025: retention premiums crowded out the attack
lessons.text: RR spent Rs 79 crore of 120 retaining six players (five batters), let Buttler, Chahal and Boult go, and finished ninth. Holding Rs 11 crore on Hetmyer and Rs 14 crore on a 38-year-old Jadeja would repeat the pattern.

lessons.title: RCB 2025: release big names, buy pressure bowlers
lessons.text: RCB kept three players, released established stars and bought Hazlewood, Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Krunal Pandya, then won their first title. All three are in our top-10 pressure bowlers.

lessons.title: RR 2022: the attack was built at the auction
lessons.text: RR kept three batters and bought Boult, Chahal, Ashwin and Prasidh Krishna; they reached the final. The purse freed here is for bowling first.

lessons.title: KKR 2024 and GT 2022: defined bowling roles win
lessons.text: Both champions had settled bowlers for each phase. No RR bowler ranks in the top 25 of 112 under pressure (Jadeja is 28th, Archer 73rd).

lessons.title: RR 2008 and the scouting edge
lessons.text: RR won the first IPL with the smallest budget by finding undervalued players. Sooryavanshi (Rs 1.1 crore), Ferreira (Rs 1 crore) and Brijesh Sharma (Rs 0.3 crore) are the 2026 version: together they return about Rs 47 crore of surplus value.
